sections.h2: Where is Greenville County and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Greenville County sits in the northwest corner of South Carolina's Upstate, against the North Carolina line. It covers 795.57 square miles, of which 785.93 are land, and the city of Greenville is both the county seat and its largest community.

The northern boundary follows the crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains, so the county reaches higher country than most of the state. The 2010 Census lists six cities: Fountain Inn, Greenville, Greer, Mauldin, Simpsonville and Travelers Rest. Fountain Inn and Greer each spill across a county line, into Laurens and Spartanburg counties.

Much of the population lives in places that are not cities at all. Taylors, Berea, Wade Hampton, Five Forks, Gantt and Slater-Marietta are census-designated places, and each has its own mix of older ranch homes, newer subdivisions and mill-era cottages.

For a seller this layout matters because a house in Travelers Rest near the mountains and a house in Mauldin near the interstate are taxed by the same county offices but sell to very different buyers.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Greenville County?
sections.html:
The state legislature created Greenville County in 1786, and the name honors General Nathanael Greene, the Revolutionary War commander of the southern campaign. The early spelling was "Greeneville."

The county grew out of the old Ninety-Six District as settlers moved into the backcountry. The census count was 6,503 in 1790 and 53,490 in 1900. By 1950 it had reached 168,152, and it has kept climbing since.

That long growth curve explains why a single county can hold homes from the 1900s, the mill villages, the postwar subdivisions and houses finished last year. Age is the first thing a cash buyer looks at when estimating repairs, and Greenville County has every age.

sections.h2: How big is Greenville County and what does its economy rely on?
sections.html:
Greenville County is the most populous county in South Carolina, with 525,534 residents in the 2020 Census and a 2025 estimate of 583,125. Its 2022 economic output was about $40.6 billion, and unemployment ran between 2.1 and 3.3 percent from 2022 to 2024.

Health care and social assistance is the largest industry by jobs, with 43,180 workers out of 292,366. Manufacturing follows with 31,693 jobs, then retail trade with 30,485.

  • Employers named for the county include Bon Secours, Charter Communications, GE Vernova, Lockheed Martin and Michelin.
  • Prisma Health, Publix, TD Bank, the Postal Service and Walmart appear on the same list.
  • Job growth in these fields draws new households, which keeps demand for starter homes steady.

A seller who relocates for work or settles an estate here is usually selling into a county where plenty of people are still arriving.

sections.h2: What roads, airports and rail serve Greenville County?
sections.html:
Interstates 85, 185 and 385 are the main highways, with US 25, 29, 123 and 276 crossing the county as well. Commute time to the jobs along those corridors is often the first thing a buyer asks about.

Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport lies mostly in Spartanburg County, while Donaldson Center Airport and Greenville Downtown Airport are inside Greenville County. Amtrak serves the city at its Greenville station.

Homes close to an interchange can sell faster to commuters, and homes on busy US routes may draw road-noise comments. A cash buyer prices those differences in, so you do not have to stage the house or wait for a buyer who likes the location.

sections.h2: When are Greenville County property taxes due, and what does a late bill cost?
sections.html:
Real property tax in Greenville County is due without penalty by January 15. Bills usually go out near the end of October, according to the county's Real Property Services calendar.

DateWhat is added
January 15Last day to pay with no penalty
January 163 percent
February 2Further 7 percent
March 17Further 5 percent plus a $15.00 execution cost

These dates match S.C. Code 12-45-180. The Tax Collector says penalties come off only when there is direct evidence of a county error.

The office is in the South Building, Suite 1100-S, and the phone is 864.467.7050. You can pay in person, by mail or online, and most payments post within three to five business days.

The county also states that the tax on a property follows the property, not the person. If you sell with the current year unpaid, the title company normally settles the balance from your proceeds.

sections.h2: How does selling a house change the assessment in Greenville County?
sections.html:
A sale is usually an assessable transfer of interest, which means the county revalues the house to a current date. Real Property Services says the 15 percent cap on increases is removed after such a transfer, and a point-of-sale reassessment uses a December 31 appraisal date for the year of the transfer.

Ownership on January 1 decides whose name is printed on the bill. If the deed changes after that date, both the old and new owners appear on that year's bill, and only the new owner appears the following year. A new assessment notice usually arrives the year after the change.

  • Owner-occupied homes get the 4 percent legal residence assessment, plus a credit that removes the school operating tax. The application must be hand-delivered or postmarked by January 15 with an original signature, and electronic filing is not accepted.
  • A buyer who will not live in the house loses that treatment, so the bill can rise sharply for the next owner.
  • The county lists a January 30 deadline for the 25 percent exemption on transfers made the previous year.

Telling your buyer about this ahead of time avoids a surprise after closing. A short call to Real Property Services at 864.467.7300 clears up anything unclear.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Greenville County assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal in writing, and the first deadline is printed on your assessment notice. If no notice was sent, the usual deadline is January 15, or the next working day if that falls on a weekend or holiday.

The statute behind this is S.C. Code 12-60-2510, which gives 90 days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more.

  1. Mail a written objection with the tax map number, your reasons and your opinion of value. Email and fax are not accepted, and the postmark decides timeliness.
  2. A certified appraiser reviews every timely appeal, and the assessor mails the result.
  3. You have 30 days from the notice of decision to protest to the County Board of Assessment Appeals.
  4. You have 30 days after the Board's written decision to go to the Administrative Law Judge Division.

Appeals go to Real Property Services at Greenville County Square, Suite 1000. The office schedules notices for new construction and other increases in late summer or early fall.

sections.h2: What happens if Greenville County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
After March 17 the bill is delinquent and the Tax Collector issues an execution notice. If the bill is still unpaid 30 days after that notice is mailed, a Notice of Seizure follows by certified mail with restricted delivery.

The sale is a public auction at the Greenville Convention Center on Exposition Drive. The sale is advertised once a week for three weeks first, and the opening bid covers all delinquent tax, penalties and costs plus the current year's tax.

The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem within 12 months. Interest on the bid is 3 percent in months one to three, 6 percent in months four to six, 9 percent in months seven to nine and 12 percent in months ten to twelve. If nobody redeems, the buyer gets a tax deed that conveys only the county's interest, not a warranty deed.

Selling before the auction is often cleaner than letting the process run. A sale closes the debt through escrow, and you avoid the redemption interest.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record the deed in Greenville County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds in Suite S-2100 of Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge, Monday to Friday from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm. The office asks you to arrive by 4:30 pm.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value or part of it, according to S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 24. The statute splits that into $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. Some transfers are exempt, including a deed in lieu of foreclosure to the mortgagee and certain family partnership or trust transfers.

Your title or escrow company normally prepares the deed and pays the fee from closing funds. If you mail a deed yourself, include a cover letter with a phone number, a stamped return envelope and a check payable to Greenville County.

faqs.q: When are Greenville County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Greenville County real property tax is due without penalty by January 15. A 3 percent penalty starts January 16, another 7 percent on February 2, and another 5 percent plus a $15.00 execution cost on March 17.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Greenville County house if the taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax follows the property, so it is paid from your sale proceeds at closing. A cash purchase can close with the balance cleared through escrow.

faqs.q: Who handles assessment appeals in Greenville County?
faqs.a: Real Property Services does, at Greenville County Square, Suite 1000, phone 864.467.7300. Objections must be in writing, and the postmark decides whether you met the deadline.

faqs.q: Does selling my home raise the next owner's tax bill?
faqs.a: Often it does. A sale is usually an assessable transfer of interest, which removes the 15 percent cap and sets a new value. The buyer also loses the 4 percent legal residence rate if the house is not their home.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a house sold at a Greenville County tax sale?
faqs.a: You have 12 months from the sale. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem by paying the taxes, penalties, costs and the stepped interest on the bid.
